title: Class imbalance and misleading accuracy, interactively
description: Course activity for Exercise 3: choose a class ratio and a predetermined split seed, then compare the logistic-regression model's test accuracy against the majority-class baseline accuracy on the same resampled cohort of real ABIDE participants -- plus AUC, balanced accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity.
instructions: Choose a class ratio (control is always the majority class here) and one of five predetermined split seeds. The chart compares the model's own test accuracy against what always-predict-control would score on the exact same test participants.
reflectionPrompts: Before moving to 95:5, predict the majority-class baseline accuracy. Then check: how close is the model's own accuracy to that baseline?
At 95:5, which of the displayed measures (AUC, balanced accuracy, sensitivity, specificity) most clearly reveals whether the model is actually detecting autistic participants?

As imbalance increases, the model's raw accuracy rises too. Is the model actually performing better than at 50:50, or worse? What might you wrongly conclude if you only saw its accuracy, without the baseline for comparison?
